upheld.reason: The two tensor factors are explicitly nonzero finite-dimensional spaces. Summing the input diagonal blocks defines the partial trace, and the spectral entropy includes zero eigenvalues by the zero-log convention. Basis independence is proved, without a converse reconstruction of joint densities.

A regulator sequence is named at every positive integer and each factor space is nonzero. The phrase sequence of nonempty sets appears only in the explanation of a conditional calibration choice axiom; the entropy definition selects no such family and asserts no empty-regulator limit.

The common frequency band has strictly positive lower endpoint and nonzero width, and each supplied packet has unit square norm. An empty support cannot satisfy normalization; the optional narrowing family is given, and the two limits are taken in the explicitly specified order.

One smooth metric family through a fixed Lorentzian background and its compactly supported inverse-metric derivative specify first-variation data. The family is parametrized by an open interval about zero, not an optional empty index collection; the pairing identities prescribe counterterm normalization, not a biconditional existence theorem. The finite-action-difference defect is separately recorded for local repair.

The coefficient index set is the fixed nonempty set of pairs of nonnegative integers, including the oscillator ground state. Parseval and the explicit positive oscillator eigenvalues control all coefficients; no optional empty orthonormal family is substituted.

The formal Ward series has a prescribed leading nilpotent differential and a first breaking order at least one. Positive-order coefficients may all vanish, but coefficient extraction still gives consistency and the relative coboundary criterion; the displayed formal series is not an optional empty family.

A finite geometric remainder on the fixed spectral band gives a vector norm bound, and Cauchy-Schwarz gives its action bound. These are upper estimates for every nonnegative energy, not necessary-and-sufficient conditions for a source to be band limited.

A unit indicator on a sufficiently high finite momentum interval lies in every required polynomial domain and violates the proposed band coefficient. This counterexample removes no hypothesis from the band-limited theorem and states no necessary-and-sufficient spectral criterion.

The normalized Kraus family explicitly has at least one member on a nonzero Hilbert space. An empty sum would be zero rather than the required identity; the commuting-family calculation does not require an additional empty-instrument branch.

The countable-family phrase records the assumed Choice consequence, not an input index set over which the kernel theorem quantifies. The fixed positive mass and unit-integral mollifier determine the heat-kernel integral, covariance convolution and logarithmic bounds; an empty family changes none of these objects.

Dual-basis independence fixes each pair Casimir, noncolliding coordinates make the logarithmic one-forms smooth, and the Leibniz calculation constructs the connection. No converse from arbitrary connections to these Lie representations is stated.

Pairwise disjoint commutators and the Arnold three-form identity make the curvature zero; the subsequent parallel frames and inverse-transport convention construct monodromy. The insertion number is at least two and a base configuration is supplied, so no empty insertion configuration is claimed.

The phrase exactly when occurs only in the required Cartan input symmetry: one off-diagonal Cartan entry is zero precisely when its transpose entry is zero. Both directions are stipulated in the matrix data; the KLR action checklist asserts neither existence nor an equivalence theorem about actions.
